correctness.rationale: The finite-dimensional spectral layer-cake expresses any positive contraction as an average of orthogonal projections. In dimension three complementary rank-one and rank-two projections have opposite strictly lower parts. The rank-one case is exhaustively parameterized by a simplex of three nonnegative weights; the squared operator norm is the largest root of an explicit characteristic quadratic, monotone in xz for each y regime. The unique sharp scalar maximum is \((1+2\sqrt2)/7\) and is attained by a real rank-one projection. Exact radical identities, characteristic polynomial, and a sampled diagnostic were executed from the included self-contained checker.

value.rationale: This is a natural positive-cone norm of the triangular Schur multiplier for Gram/covariance matrices and ordered iterative solvers. Three dimensions is the first case where two levels of strictly lower-triangular interactions yield a sharp ratio above 1/2. The exact constant and explicit Gram extremizer are not a renaming of an unrestricted operator norm, and the proof gives a transferable projection-reduction strategy. No higher-dimensional theorem is claimed or needed to make this finite sharp inequality informative.
